correctness.rationale: On a tree an edge forms a surviving two-patch component with probability p²(1−p)^{deg u+deg v−2}; polynomial coefficients give c_s. Subcubic inverse solves all m_ij explicitly. For Δ<=4 the difference kernel is exactly t(0,-1,1,1,-1,-1,1,0,0); nonzero t forces n2>=2,n3>=2,n4>=1,n1>=6 and hence n>=11. Two explicit 11-vertex trees meet this bound with equal (n_i)=(6,2,2,1), equal (c3..c8)=(1,3,4,1,1,0), and differing joint degree tables. Independent full 2048-subset enumeration confirmed expectation 59/128 at p=1/2 and entire witness counts. Analytical kernel proves minimality over all trees.

originality.rationale: Qualified PASS: The full M-polynomial is known and plainly determines edge-degree counts, but the observed polynomial is only its diagonal specialization. Known joint-degree-matrix realization theorems take all m_ij as input and do not prove recovery or minimal loss from diagonal counts. Valence-connectivity plus multiple Zagreb/Randić indices are richer measurements. No located prior result gives this sharp 11-node degree-four threshold; specialized chemical graph equivalent remains a risk.
residual_risks: Exact degree-sum polynomial inversion may occur under alternative chemical graph-index vocabulary.
No claim that the observable reconstructs a labeled graph or works with noisy observations.

value.rationale: The inverse problem of recovering edge-class connectivity from an observable random-fragment expectation plus degree census is natural. A complete subcubic guarantee, unique ambiguity direction at degree four, and sharp minimal 11-patch counterexample quantify an important identifiability boundary.

limitations: Assumes tree, homogeneous independent survival and separate exact degree census.
Sharp 11-node claim only among trees with max degree <=4.
Exact degree-sum polynomial inversion may occur under alternative chemical graph-index vocabulary.
No claim that the observable reconstructs a labeled graph or works with noisy observations.
